summary: Establish a replay-safe, tenant-scoped ClickHouse analytical projection and query boundary while keeping PostgreSQL/EventBus authoritative and forbidding unsourced cross-currency aggregation.

impacts.evidence: Every ingest batch is restricted to one organization/workspace and every QueryPort call requires validated tenancy.Scope; ClickHouse views retain both identifiers as leading query keys.

Only order_changed and stock_changed payloads are admitted in Task 049; all other event bodies become an empty JSON object while bounded envelope metadata supplies freshness. Task 061 owns retention and coordinated deletion.
No public HTTP/OpenAPI operation is added. Reporting reads are introduced as an internal provider-neutral QueryPort for later application/API work.
Task 049 consumes existing canonical EventBus envelopes and adds no event type or payload version.
Connector SDK/provider roots are unchanged; reporting is a host-side analytical port and imports no provider implementation.
A ClickHouse-only schema creates replayable event/order/inventory/freshness projections. No PostgreSQL migration is added because PostgreSQL remains truth and ClickHouse can be rebuilt.
Analytical payloads are allow-listed/minimized, cross-tenant batches fail closed, query scope is mandatory, and ClickHouse is never an authorization or transactional-write authority.
Task 049 is read-only analytics. It explicitly forbids target-currency totals and other derived financial actions until Task 089b has sourced historical FX provenance.
Each analytical record preserves event_id/type/entity/source plus replay and source-position provenance. event_id remains semantic identity across retries and full rebuilds.

Exact batches have deterministic retry tokens; semantic materialized projections use uniqExact/argMax state so repeated EventBus delivery or replay cannot inflate initial sales, inventory or freshness results. Replay checkpoints advance only after sink acknowledgement.
Task 049 adds no webhook ingress/egress or provider network surface.
freshness_v1 and QueryPort expose distinct event count, last occurrence, last durable ingest and source lag per event family; Tasks 066 and 077 consume these signals later.
ClickHouse objects are disposable derived state. Rollback/recovery recreates the prior schema and replays authoritative events; transactional PostgreSQL recovery never waits for ClickHouse.

Tests cover tenant isolation, deterministic batch identity, replay idempotency, checkpoint no-progress failure, latest inventory state, original-currency sales, freshness lag and static ClickHouse replay/currency invariants.
